name: Iddo
overview: Iddo was a male leader from the tribe of Manasseh, serving as a chief officer for the Manassehites in Gilead. He is specifically identified as the son of Zechariah. His role as a chief officer highlights his position of authority within his tribe during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles.
namesAndTitles: The name Iddo is a proper name that likely means 'YHWH has adorned.' This meaning reflects a possible divine blessing or favor, though the name was not given directly by God according to the record in 1 Chronicles 27:21.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Iddo was the son of Zechariah. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Iddo's significance lies in his leadership role among the Manassehites in Gilead, indicating his trusted status in tribal governance or military affairs during the time chronicled in 1 Chronicles. His mention alongside his father Zechariah situates him within a notable lineage, emphasizing the continuity of leadership within his family. Though brief, his record contributes to the broader understanding of tribal organization and leadership in Israel's history.
